chunks: Hadith 5593 — Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام made this charity-endowment: “This is what Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام has given as charity. He gave in charity all of his land in such-and-such a place, and the boundary of the land is such-and-such. He gave all of it in charity, together with its palm trees, its land, its canal, its water, its mills, its rights, its watering share from the water, and every right belonging to it in elevation or exposure, width or length, utility, open area, watercourses, branches, runoff, cultivated or uncultivated land. He gave all his rights in that as charity for his direct offspring among men and women. Its administrator shall distribute what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings forth of its yield, in the amount sufficient for its upkeep and its utilities; after thirty date-clusters, he shall distribute among the needy of the village and among the children of so-and-so.”
“For the male is the like of the share of two females.”

If a woman from the daughters of so-and-so marries, then she has no right from this charity-endowment until she returns to it without a husband. If she returns, then she shall have the like of the share of one of the daughters of so-and-so who did not marry. And whoever dies among the children of so-and-so and has a child, then his child has his father’s share.
“For the male is the like of the share of two females.”

According to what so-and-so stipulated among his direct offspring. And whoever dies among the children of so-and-so and leaves no child behind, his right is returned to the people of the charity-endowment. And the children of my daughters have no right in this charity-endowment unless their fathers are from my offspring. And no one has any right in my charity-endowment along with my children, the children of my children, and their descendants so long as any of them remain. If they pass away and none of them remain, that shall be divided among the children of my father through my mother, so long as any of them remain, according to the like of what I stipulated among my children and my descendants. Then when the children of my father through my mother pass away and none of them remain, my charity-endowment is for the children of my father and their descendants, so long as any of them remain, according to the like of what I stipulated among my children and my descendants. Then when the children of my father pass away and none of them remain, my charity-endowment is for the nearer and then the nearer, until Allah inherits it—He who inherited it—and He is the best of inheritors.

And the Abode of the Hereafter. It is not lawful for a believer who believes in Allah and the Last Day to sell it, buy it, gift it, transfer it, or alter anything from it until Allah inherits “the earth and those upon it.” He placed this charity-endowment under 'Ali and Ibrahim. Then if one of the two passes away, al-Qasim joins the one remaining. Then if one of them passes away, Isma'il joins the one remaining of them. Then if one of them passes away, al-'Abbas joins the one remaining of them. Then if one of them passes away, the eldest of my children joins the one remaining of them. And if none remains of my children with him except one, then he is the one who takes charge of it.

key_terms.أَرْضِهِ: his land that is being donated as an endowment
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةِ: the endowed charity property being permanently dedicated
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the Hereafter as the intended divine-oriented purpose
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the earth, in the quoted eschatological expression of ultimate divine inheritance
key_terms.حُقُوقِهَا: the appurtenant rights and legal entitlements attached to the property
key_terms.عَقِبِي: my progeny or lineal descendants after my children
key_terms.غَلَّتِهَا: the produce or yield generated from the endowed land

ai.seo_question: What conditions did Imam Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام set for his charitable endowment and its inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith records the detailed terms of a charitable endowment established by Imam Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, specifying the endowed property, its beneficiaries, rules of distribution, succession, and administration. It is significant as a legal text on waqf-like charity, inheritance-style allocation among descendants, and the perpetual protection of endowed property from sale, transfer, or alteration.
